what: Tenable sells exposure management software: tools that scan an organisation’s computers, cloud services and networks for vulnerabilities and rank which ones to fix first. Its Nessus scanner is one of the most widely used security tools in the world.
customers: Corporate security teams and governments, from small businesses to large enterprises.
money: Tenable One, Tenable Vulnerability Management and cloud security, sold as recurring subscriptions.
moat: Nessus is the industry standard for vulnerability scanning, which gives Tenable a large installed base to sell its broader platform into.
risks: Growth has slowed to about 10% a year as larger platforms bundle vulnerability management.
GAAP profit is near zero because of stock compensation; equity is negative after buybacks.
Consolidation in security favours large platforms such as CrowdStrike and Palo Alto.
opportunities: Free cash flow grew from $93M in 2021 to $280M over the last twelve months.
The forward P/E of about 19 is low for security software.
Exposure management for AI and cloud assets is a growing need.
It could be an acquisition target for a larger platform.
watch: Annual recurring revenue growth and free cash flow margin.
view: Tenable is a profitable, cash-generating security company growing about 10% a year, with free cash flow of $280 million over the last twelve months. The GAAP P/E of 348 is meaningless because of stock compensation; on free cash flow, the market value of $4.7 billion is about 17 times.

That is cheap for security software, and it reflects the market’s fear that big platforms will bundle what Tenable sells. CrowdStrike’s purchase of Zscaler shows how fast the industry is consolidating, and standalone vendors risk being squeezed.

This turns on growth. If Tenable can hold around 10% and expand margins, the shares are inexpensive, and a takeover is plausible. If growth slows further, the discount is justified. I think it is reasonably priced with some takeover optionality.
bull: Exposure management grows with AI and cloud, margins expand and a larger buyer emerges.
bear: Platform bundling erodes growth and Tenable becomes a slow-growing niche vendor.
